guide.title: Drowning & Submersion Injury
guide.lead: Drowning is a breathing problem. The fix is oxygen: start rescue breaths as soon as it's safe, give ventilation priority in CPR, and never waste time draining water. Anyone with symptoms afterwards goes to hospital, because they can worsen over hours.

sections.title: Rescue safely
items: Reach, throw, row – then go (trained rescuers only)
Spinal care only if there's a diving, fall or high-energy mechanism, or signs of injury
Cold water: limit your own time in it

figures.alt: Reach, throw, row, go: four small panels – a pole, a throw bag, a boat, and a trained swimmer with a flotation device.

steps.title: Open the airway and breathe
steps.text: Start with rescue breaths: 5 initial breaths (ERC). Suction only what blocks the airway.

figures.alt: A rescuer on a pool deck giving bag-mask breaths to a child, foam at the mouth, suction ready beside them.

steps.title: No signs of life
steps.text: CPR with ventilations: 30:2 adults; 15:2 children with two rescuers. Oxygen as soon as possible.

steps.title: Breathing but not adequately
steps.text: Bag-mask ventilation; child: 1 breath every 2–3 seconds; adult: 1 every 6 seconds.

steps.title: Advanced airway
steps.text: Early if ventilation is hard; expect foam – keep ventilating through it.

steps.title: Vomit
steps.text: Common: turn to the side, suction, continue.

sections.title: Don't
items: Abdominal thrusts to 'drain' water: they cause vomiting and delay breaths
Worry about fresh vs salt water: care is the same
Stop early in ice-water submersion, especially in children

sections.title: Who goes to hospital?
items: Anyone who needed rescue breaths or CPR
Any cough, foam, breathlessness, abnormal lung sounds, SpO₂ below 95% or altered mental status
"Dry" or "secondary" drowning are no longer recognised terms: symptoms start early and can worsen over hours

items.label: Hypoxic bradycardia
items.sub: Ventilate: the heart rate usually rises with oxygen.

items.label: Asystole
items.sub: The usual drowning arrest rhythm: CPR with good ventilations.

quiz.q: 3-year-old pulled from a pool after 3–4 minutes: unresponsive, not breathing, no pulse. First?
options: Open the airway and give rescue breaths, then CPR with strong ventilations
quiz.explanation: Hypoxia caused the arrest; oxygen fixes it.

quiz.q: Adult rescued after 2 minutes underwater: alert, coughing, frothy sputum, SpO₂ 91%. He wants to go home. You:
options: Explain he needs hospital: symptoms can worsen over hours
quiz.explanation: Cough and low SpO₂ mean lung injury.

quiz.q: Child pulled from an icy pond after about 20 minutes: pulseless. You:
options: Full resuscitation with rewarming: cold-water submersion has had good outcomes
quiz.explanation: Transport to a centre with ECLS if possible.

options: Rescue breathing is the priority; no abdominal thrusts
Fresh and salt water need different care

quiz.q: Bag-mask rate for a child with a pulse but inadequate breathing:
Spinal motion restriction after drowning is needed when:
options: There is a diving, fall or high-energy mechanism or signs of injury

quiz.q: The usual cardiac arrest rhythm after drowning:
Foam pouring from the airway during ventilation. You:
options: Keep ventilating through it; suction only what blocks
quiz.explanation: Foam is fluid from the lungs; it will keep coming.

A sudden death days later without symptoms

flashcards.question: Definition of drowning
flashcards.answer: Respiratory impairment from submersion or immersion in liquid. Outcomes: death, or survival with or without injury. "Dry", "wet" and "secondary" drowning are outdated terms.

flashcards.question: Priority in drowning
flashcards.answer: Ventilation. Rescue breaths as soon as safe; ventilation-first CPR; oxygen early.

flashcards.question: Who goes to hospital?
flashcards.answer: Anyone who needed breaths or CPR, or has cough, foam, breathlessness, abnormal lung sounds, low SpO₂ or altered mental status. Symptoms can worsen over hours.

flashcards.question: Fresh vs salt water
flashcards.answer: Different lung mechanisms, identical prehospital care: oxygen and ventilation.

flashcards.question: Diving reflex
flashcards.answer: Cold water on the face slows the heart and shunts blood to the brain and heart; strongest in children. One reason for good outcomes after ice-water submersion.

flashcards.question: Drowning sequence
flashcards.answer: Breath-holding and panic, laryngospasm, then aspiration as hypoxia deepens, lung injury, bradycardia, arrest.

flashcards.question: Abdominal thrusts in drowning?
flashcards.answer: No: they cause vomiting and aspiration and delay ventilation. Water in the lungs is absorbed.

flashcards.question: Drowning management steps
flashcards.answer: Safe rescue; spinal care only for trauma; airway and breaths; CPR emphasising ventilation; remove wet clothes and warm; hospital for anyone symptomatic.

critical.scenario: 4-year-old pulled from a pool 2 minutes ago: unresponsive, not breathing, weak carotid pulse about 50/min.
critical.question: Management?

options.t: Bag-mask with oxygen at 1 breath every 2–3 seconds; if HR stays below 60 with poor perfusion, start CPR; no abdominal thrusts

critical.explanation: Hypoxic bradycardia usually responds to ventilation.
critical.kpi: Provides pediatric rescue breathing for drowning with bradycardia

critical.scenario: 22-year-old pulled from a river after 5–7 minutes underwater; friends were drinking and swimming. Pulseless, apnoeic.
critical.question: Sequence and special considerations?

options.t: Rescue breaths first, then CPR with good ventilations; suction vomit, early advanced airway, oxygen; consider injury if he dived; warm and transport

options.f: Ventilation is the key in drowning.

critical.explanation: Alcohol and diving raise the chance of a neck injury.

critical.scenario: 7-year-old pool drowning, intubated by the first crew, still in arrest. Absent left breath sounds, distended neck veins, trachea deviated to the right; ventilation getting harder.
critical.question: What is happening?

options.t: Left tension pneumothorax from ventilation: needle decompression on the left per protocol, then reassess tube position

options.f: That causes absent left sounds but not a deviated trachea and distended veins.

critical.explanation: Also check DOPE: displacement, obstruction, pneumothorax, equipment.
critical.kpi: Recognizes tension pneumothorax during drowning resuscitation
